3.     PUBLIC HEARINGS


        a)   BYLAW NO. 1717
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 507, (2500 Echo Valley Dr), 2017".


The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1717 at 5:32 p.m.

Acting Mayor M. Sahlstrom advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that
his or her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the
matters contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw
should give their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. The Acting Mayor advised that
after everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to
be heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                                           March 19th, 2018
                                                                                               Page 2 of 14



The City Planner advised that Rachael Sansom of Turner Lane Development Corp. has applied on
behalf of 1085540 BC Ltd. to amend the text of "Area 2" in the CD6 (Comprehensive Development
6 — Bear Mountain) Zone to allow for a townhouse development at 2500 Echo Valley Drive.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the
Local Government Act. In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the
following items prior to Public Hearing:


1. A detailed site plan illustrating two routes for access to and egress from the site;
2. A stormwater management plan; and
3.   Confirmation of adequate water, fire flow and sanitary sewer capacities to serve the
      proposed development; and


The applicant has submitted the required access plan, and a Servicing Feasibility Study to the
satisfaction of the Director of Engineering (it should be noted that the study has been approved
for conceptual stormwater management only, all other servicing is subject to detailed design
approval. Detailed stormwater calculations will be required during site servicing and will be
subject to further approvals by the City).


The applicant has also agreed to provide a Section 219 Covenant, prior to Bylaw Adoption,
addressing frontage improvements, stormwater management, water supply, road access to
adjacent properties, local service agreements and firefighting provisions.


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Hillside or Shoreline designation.
Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.


Concurrent with this application, Council may also wish to consider discharging a Covenant
registered as a condition of rezoning for the properties located at 1410 Grand Forest Close, 1431
Grand Forest Close and 2342 Lairds Gate which are adjacent to the subject property.                  This
Covenant was registered at the request of the previous owner of 2500 Echo Valley Drive in order
to restrict development of these adjacent properties to minimize the potential impact of
development on the property at 2500 Echo Valley Drive.


Ownership of 2500 Echo Valley has since changed, and the new owner wishes to develop the
property as evidenced by this application. Council may therefore wish to discharge the Covenant
on 1410 Grand Forest Close, 1431 Grand Forest Close and 2342 Lairds Gate in advance of the 5
year timeline expiry date.

None presented.

             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 509, (2869 Sooke Rd Portion), 2018".

Acting Mayor M. Sahlstrom advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that
his or her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the
matters contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw

advised that after everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else
who wishes to be heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared

The City Planner advised that Mr. Richard Irwin applied on behalf of 89 Chicken Ranch Ltd to amend the
zoning of 3370, 3344 Luxton Road and 2869 Sooke Road from the from RR2 (Rural Residential 2) Zone to
Business Park 2A — Sooke Road West (BP2A) Zone, the Bylaw associated with this amendment was
adopted by Council at their December 8th, 2017 meeting.


A condition of this Zoning amendment was the closure of Luxton Road between Marwood Avenue and
Sooke Road. In order to facilitate traffic flow along the new extension of Marwood Avenue that would
connect to Sooke Road through the subject property.


The portion of Luxton Road will stay open until the new road is fully operational, however, the developer
would like to amend this portion of road so as it can be integrated into the development plans of the
adjacent parcel once the road is closed.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

source_identity.raw_motion_text:
That Development Variance Permit No. DVP17-0023 be issued by the Council for the City of Langford
to Dan Hodge on behalf of Dan and Munirih Hodge to reduce the minimum rear yard setback from 6.0 m
(20 ft) to 2.7 m (9 ft) and defer the requirement for the installation of on-site plumbing to allow for the
construction of an addition to the existing one-family dwelling at 2579 Rainville Road subject to the
following terms and conditions:



1.   Appendix


     The site shall be developed in accordance with the site plan attached (Appendix A).

                                                                                                  March 19th, 2018
                                                                                                      Page 6 of 14




2.    Variances


      The following regulations of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 are varied under Section 498 of the Local
      Government Act:

      a)   That Section 6.21.06(1)(a) of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 be varied to reduce the minimum setback from
           the rear lot line from 6.0 m (20 ft) to 2.7 m (9 ft); and
      b)   That Section 6.1.2(c) of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied to defer
           the installation of on-site plumbing from prior to the issuance of an Occupancy Permit for the
           proposed addition to within six months of a sewer main being installed in a highway or City
           statutory right-of-way abutting the property at 2579 Rainville Road;

3.    Conditions

      The following requirements are imposed under Section 498 of the Local Government Act:


      I.  That the site is developed in substantial accordance with the plans attached to this report as
          Appendix C;
      II. That the owner registers a Section 219 Covenant, in priority of all other charges, prior to the
          issuance of this Development Variance Permit that agrees that all required on-site plumbing will
          be installed and connected to the municipal sanitary sewer system within six months of a sewer
          main being installed in a highway or City statutory right-of-way abutting the parcel;
     III. That the owner pays the required Sewer Capital Recovery Fee (SCRF) to West Shore
          Environmental Services or the City of Langford prior to the issuance of a Building Permit
          authorizing the construction of the proposed addition at 2579 Rainville Road; and
     IV. That the owner provides confirmation of adequate septic field capacity for the proposed
          addition containing a shop and secondary suite from Island Health prior to the issuance of a
          Building Permit authorizing the construction of the proposed addition at 2579 Rainville Road.

That Council:

                                                                                                March 19th, 2018
                                                                                                    Page 7 of 14




1.   Give 1st reading to the attached Bylaw No. 1767 to amend the zoning designation of the properties
     located at 2682, 2684, 2686, 2696, 2702, and 2706 Sooke Road from District Commercial (C3) and
     Service Commercial (CS1) to a new Community Town Centre Pedestrian 9 (C9) zone subject to the
     following terms and conditions:


         a)   That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions
              per residential unit, prior to issuance of a building permit:

                 i.   $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund, and either
                 ii. $2,074 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund, OR
                 iii. Full road improvements for the realignment of Glen Lake Road


         b) That the applicant provides, prior to public hearing, the following:

                 i.    A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately
                       managed for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director of
                       Engineering.


         c)   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered
              in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

                 i.    That the owner will not apply for, nor is the City obligated to issue a Development
                       Permit, Building Permit, or Subdivision until the road (as shown) has been
                       dedicated.
                ii.    That at any time after the 5th anniversary date of adoption of the bylaw to rezone
                       the subject lands, that the City may request, and the owner shall provide, the area
                       of land necessary for the construction of the road extension from Happy Valley
                       Road to Glen Lake Road as well as Sooke Road for $1.00.
                iii.   That the owner will limit direct vehicular access to Sooke Road, and will not apply
                       for, nor will the City be obligated to grant driveway access on to Sooke Road,
                       except in accordance with a comprehensive plan of development for the
                       properties as a whole.
                iv.    That the owner will provide an easement for reciprocal vehicular access in
                       conjunction with any Development Permit where various properties may be
                       affected, to the satisfaction of the City Planner.
                v.     That a Traffic Impact Assessment (TIA) be completed to the satisfaction of the
                       Director of Engineering for the full build-out of any block that commercial and/or
                       residential uses are proposed, prior to the issuance of building permit, and that
                       the recommendations of the TIA be implemented prior to Occupancy of any
                       buildings;
               vi.     That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards are provided to the
                       satisfaction of the Director of Engineering and Manager of Parks prior to issuance
                       of a building permit; and
               vii.    That a detailed storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a
                       building permit and implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the
                       Director of Engineering.

                                                                                                    March 19th, 2018
                                                                                                        Page 8 of 14


   2.   Direct the City Planner to permit onsite parking, through the Development Permit for Form and
        Character, to be at a ratio of 1.0 stall per 1 or 2 bedroom units, with any additional 0.25 for visitor
        parking.


   3.   Direct the City Planner to permit onsite parking and loading facilities, through the Development
        Permit for Form and Character, to be located in the front or side yards for buildings located
        immediately next to the Galloping Goose.

source_identity.raw_motion_text:
That Council:

   1.   Give First Reading of Bylaw 1762, a Bylaw to amend the zoning designation of the property located
        at 2158 Millstream Road from the R2 (One and Two Family Residential) Zone to the RS4
        (Residential Small Lot 4) Zone, subject to the following terms and conditions:


            a)   That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following
                 contributions per lot, prior to issuance of a building permit:


                   i.    $3,960 per small lot single family home towards the General Amenity Reserve
                         Fund less the cost to construct the additional 77.4 m of sidewalk beyond the
                         property frontage;
                   ii.   $660 per small lot single family home towards the Affordable Housing Reserve
                         Fund;


            b)   That the developer provides, prior to Public Hearing the following:

                    i.   A technical Stormwater Management Memo to the satisfaction of the Director of
                         Engineering;


            c)   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered
                 in priority of all other charges on title that agrees to the following:


                   1.    That the developer agrees to implement the approved storm water management
                         plan and to complete any required improvements and/or upgrades to on site and
                         off site infrastructure necessary to facilitate proper drainage on the subject
                         property at the developer's expense;
                   ii.   That the developer will construct full frontage improvements, including, but not
                         limited to, boulevard planting, and light standards within the frontages of all
                         internal roads and along the Millstream Road frontage. The installation of

                                                                                                March 19th, 2018
                                                                                                    Page 9 of 14



                      sidewalks on one side of internal roads as well as along the frontage of Millstream
                      Road that connects the entrance of Bear Mountain Parkway to Nirwan Place. All
                      frontage improvements shall be in accordance with Bylaw No.1000 and to the
                      satisfaction of the Director of Engineering. These improvements shall be installed
                      prior to subdivision approval or building permit issuance, whichever is first, or be
                      the subject of a development servicing agreement to the satisfaction of the
                      Director of Engineering;
               iii.   That any necessary above or underground infrastructure or servicing upgrades,
                      extensions or other required servicing requirements are to be fulfilled to the
                      standards of Bylaw No. 1000 and the Director of Engineering, and that costs
                      incurred will be the responsibility of the developer;
               iv.    That the developer agrees to register a road dedication along Millstream Road
                      as is necessary to accommodate any and all required frontage improvements
                      prior to the issuance of any building permits or subdivision approvals, whichever
                      is first, on the Lands;
                v.    That developer agrees to register statutory right of way over the utility corridor
                      to serve as a pedestrian path connection to Bear Mountain Parkway, prior to the
                      issuance of any building permits or subdivision approvals, whichever is first, on
                      the Lands;
               vi.    That the developer agrees to construct a pedestrian path, approximately 4 m
                      wide and 30 m long that is accessible and inclusive to those with mobility issues,
                      to the satisfaction of the Manager of Parks and Recreation, prior to the issuance
                      of any building permits on the Lands;
               vii.   That the applicant will submit a construction parking management plan, to the
                      satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to building permit issuance;
              viii.   That the developer will endeavor to alert the future property owners of the
                      proximity to Western Speed Way Recreation Park, and the nuisance this location
                      may cause;
                ix.   To extend the sidewalk from Bear Mountain Parkway to Niwan Place, an
                      additional 77.4 m of sidewalk that is not within the subject property frontage.
                x.    That the applicant submit FUS calculations to the satisfaction of the Director of
                      Engineering prior to subdivision approval or building permit issuance, whichever
                      is first.

                      satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to building permit issuance;
              viii.   That the developer will endeavor to alert the future property owners of the
                      proximity to Western Speed Way Recreation Park, and the nuisance this location
                      may cause;
                ix.   To extend the sidewalk from Bear Mountain Parkway to Niwan Place, an
                      additional 77.4 m of sidewalk that is not within the subject property frontage.
                x.    That the applicant submit FUS calculations to the satisfaction of the Director of
                      Engineering prior to subdivision approval or building permit issuance, whichever
